saints.name: St. Junípero Serra
saints.title: Priest and Missionary
saints.shortBlurb: The Franciscan friar who founded the first missions of California and is called its apostle…
biography: Born Miguel José Serra on 24 November 1713 at Petra in Majorca, he entered the Friars Minor at Palma in 1730, taking the name Junípero after the lowly companion of Francis. Ordained in 1737, he held the Duns Scotus chair of philosophy at the Lullian University before begging leave for the American missions in 1749, walking from Veracruz to Mexico City on a leg that never healed.

After eight years among the Pame of the Sierra Gorda, he was named president of the Baja California missions when the Jesuits were expelled in 1767, and in 1769 joined the Portolá expedition north, founding Mission San Diego de Alcalá on 16 July. In fifteen years, on a crippled leg, he founded nine missions from San Diego to San Francisco, headquartered at Mission San Carlos Borromeo in Carmel.

He died at Carmel on 28 August 1784. Beatified by John Paul II in 1988, he was canonized by Pope Francis on 23 September 2015 at Washington, the first canonization on American soil. Called the Apostle of California, he is patron of that state, of Hispanic Americans, and of vocations, for the zeal that carried a professor to the ends of the earth.
saints.knownFor: Founding the California missions and evangelizing its native peoples.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Junípero Serra (vatican.va)
